newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's Alba expects to produce 500,000 t in 97.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's Alba expects to produce 500,000 t in 97.

text.p: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), the Middle East's biggest aluminium producer, said on Monday it expected to produce 500,000 tonnes in 1997, buoyed by the end of an expansion project and an upgrading in the smelter.
"We are looking to reach 500,000 tonnes by the end of 1997. We expect to hit that target this year," Alba's senior public relations officer David Lloyd told Reuters.
Lloyd said a $130 million expansion project and upgrading had been completed in March, 10 weeks ahead of schedule. It added 36,500 tonnes to its annual production capacity of 460,000 tonnes, he said.

"Line 3 expansion was up and running at full capacity of 25,000 tonnes a year in March...all 76 cells have come on stream in March," Lloyd said. "Upgrading of line 3 gave another 11,500 tonnes. Therefore, it gave us a total of 36,500 tonnes per annum."
Alba awarded ABB Kraftwerke, part of Asea Brown Boveri AG, a $58.5 million contract in 1995 to install a 146-megawatt gas turbine and associated equipment as part of the overall expansion.

Alba, which produced around 460,000 tonnes in 1996, is 77 percent owned by the Bahraini government and 20 percent by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. German group Breton Investments holds the rest.
